$comment: Plain-language meaning of each permission and entitlement. The usage strings and entitlement keys come from apps/ios/Project.swift and apps/ios/Resources/MacHardenedRuntime.entitlements (scripts/generate.ts); each needs an entry here. Runtime prompts quote the code that asks for them.

usage.NSCameraUsageDescription: Camera: asked the first time you scan a pairing QR code or take a photo to send.
usage.NSMicrophoneUsageDescription: Microphone: asked the first time you use voice input. Audio is transcribed on the device.
usage.NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription: Photos (add only): asked the first time you save a picture from a conversation. Yorozu can't read your library through this.
usage.NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription: Local Network: asked after you tap Continue on "Connect directly on Wi-Fi?" (iPhone, iPad, and Mac on macOS 15 or later), so the app can reach your host directly on the same network. Denied or off, it uses the relay, loopback and Tailscale; Settings › Host › Direct on Local Network turns it on or off.

entitlements.aps-environment: Push notifications through Apple's service. Nothing to grant; the notification prompt below decides whether they show.
entitlements.com.apple.developer.associated-domains: Opens the app from https://yorozu.yumi.to/pair links (the pairing QR's web link).
entitlements.keychain-access-groups: Keeps the pairing keys in the Keychain, shared with the app's own extensions only.
entitlements.com.apple.security.application-groups: A container shared with the app's own extensions (share sheet, voice model download).
entitlements.com.apple.security.device.audio-input: Lets the hardened-runtime Mac app use the microphone for voice input. macOS still asks you first.

runtime.name: Notifications
runtime.meaning: Asked right after pairing. On iPhone and iPad it allows push for replies while the app is closed; on the Mac, local notifications while the app runs (the Mac gets no push). Settings › General › Notifications shows the state and opens the system settings.
